source: The three live retrospective failures recorded on 2026-10-02, after the compact answer shape went live (w3-retrocompact, live from cint-L25). PROVENANCE, field by field. Everything under `recorded` is copied verbatim from real journals through the Studio read-only file route on 2026-10-02 from the Mama PC: `recorded.justinRoot` is the retrospective projection of .instar/lanes/pipeline/live-proof/results/retrolive-evidence-20261002/justin-retrospective-status.json (Justin's preview root, passes 0-13); `recorded.freshRoot` is the same projection of room2-fresh-root-retrospective-status.json (proof room two's fresh root, its very first pass at 09:28); `recorded.proofChecks` are the FAIL lines of group-I.out, group-O.out and group-P.out from the same directory. Nothing here is authored: every number, state and reason string is the live record. The answers replayed against these shapes in retrospective-first-pass-fit.test.ts are authored, because no model has been asked for the shape this unit introduces, and the first live pass is its real proof.

liveIdShapes.note: Live case ids, taken from the live journal's own id grammar (tests/preview/fixtures/proofroom-memory-misfire-715672853-2026-09-30.json carries update 715672853 of bot 8475132199). A fixture id is far shorter, which is why this estimate must be measured against live-length ids.

liveModelRuns.note: Four REAL retrospective calls through the production prepared ask (prepareJournalEnvelope + the subscription conversation policy's own argv and system prompt), on this unit's fixture root, claude-sonnet-4-5, 2026-10-02 on the Mama PC. Driven by scripts/retro-live-model-run.mjs; the verbatim prepared prompt, provider frame and extracted answer of each call are kept beside this branch's report. `plannedBytes` is the pass's own estimatedAnswerBytes, `outputTokens` the provider frame's own count (what the route's output cap counts), `answerBytes` the extracted Decision conclusion, and `frameBytes` the whole Decision text. The frame carries the model's reasoning in reason.value beside the answer, which is why plannedBytes per output token is far below a reply's bytes per token. HONESTY: three of the four fitted the route's output cap and one did not — run4 call 2 reported 2133 output tokens against a cap of 2048. It was planned at 3459 bytes under the old reply-measured ratio, and that run's provider stub did not enforce the cap, so the pass recorded complete where the real route would have refused the frame. It is the calibration datum for the corrected ratio, not a success.
